questions.question: At a railroad crossing during your driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of your vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During your driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, you will:

options.text: Fail only that exercise.
Lose an extra point from your final score.
Automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: If students cause a disturbance on the bus while other students are getting off, you should:

options.text: Walk to the back of the bus right away to handle the problem while students exit.
Wait until all students have exited, then handle the disturbance.
Have a nearby student handle it while you watch the unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students have exited, then handle the disturbance.
questions.explanation: You must focus completely on loading and unloading students. If there is a behavior problem, wait until all students have safely exited the bus before you address it.

questions.question: After students get off at school, you should:

options.text: Not worry about where the students go.
Leave after the students have entered the school building.
Walk through the bus to check for sleeping or hiding students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for sleeping or hiding students.
questions.explanation: After students exit at school, walk through the bus to check for sleeping students, students hiding on the bus, and items left behind. Watch students as they exit in an orderly way.

questions.question: If a student drops something while walking to the school bus, the student should:

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Ask another student to pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: If a student bends down to pick up a dropped item, the driver may not be able to see them. This is dangerous. Students should move away from the bus to a safe spot, get the driver's attention, and let the driver pick up the item.

questions.question: If you must drive in high winds, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Drive faster.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: A school bus can be pushed by strong winds because of its large sides. In windy conditions, grip the steering wheel firmly, expect wind gusts, and slow down. Contact your dispatcher if you need help deciding whether to continue driving.

questions.question: When picking up students for a school bus:

options.text: Students should wait at an official bus stop.
The driver should stop anywhere to pick up students walking to a bus stop.
Parents can decide where the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at an official bus stop.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers can only pick up students at official bus stops that have been approved by school officials.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are nearby.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during your driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror on a school bus is used to:

options.text: Watch the passengers.
Look at the outside of the bus.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the passengers.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror watches passenger activity inside the bus. Adjust it so you can see every student, including those sitting right behind you.

questions.question: To safely exit a school bus, students should:

options.text: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
Stand up and walk toward the door as the bus slows down.
Exit and stand next to the bus while it drives away from the stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
questions.explanation: Students should stay seated until the driver says it is safe to exit. After leaving the bus, walk at least 10 feet away so the driver can clearly see you.

questions.question: If the driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what will happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything about a crossing.
You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the correct railroad crossing procedures at a practice location.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror located?

options.text: On the outside left of the bus.
On the outside right of the bus.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: In a school bus, the overhead rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides whether to proceed?

options.text: The driver.
A control device indicates the decision.
The vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control device. The driver alone decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: Do school buses have anti-lock braking systems (ABS)?

options.text: No, they are never equipped with ABS.
Only in cold climates.
Some are equipped with ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some are equipped with ABS.
questions.explanation: Most buses made after 1998 or 1999 must have anti-lock braking systems. Many older buses also have them.

questions.question: Where are a school bus's danger zones located?

options.text: Only in front of the bus.
Only at the rear and left side of the bus.
At the front, sides, and rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the front, sides, and rear of the bus.
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children can be hit by the bus or another vehicle. They are located at the front, sides, and rear of the bus. These zones extend up to 10 feet from all sides of the bus.

questions.question: If the driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what will happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything about a crossing.
You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the correct procedures at a practice location.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items.
The same way each time so you do not forget anything.
Once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you do not forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way before every drive. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you check everything.

questions.question: When asked to make a turn during the driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use a turn signal since you were told to make the turn.
Check traffic only to your right.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during the test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: When properly adjusted, flat mirrors on a school bus should allow the driver to see how far behind the bus?

options.text: 50 feet
100 feet
200 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet
questions.explanation: Proper mirror adjustment is important for safe bus operation. Flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet, or four bus lengths, behind the bus.

questions.question: When should you adjust a bus's mirrors?

options.text: Before operating the bus.
While operating the bus.
At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before operating the bus.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you start driving.
